# Clipboard History

> Free, open-source clipboard manager for macOS — brings back recently copied text, links, rich text, direct PNG/TIFF images, and Finder items with Shift+Command+V (customizable). Keeps the last 1,000 copies by default (up to 10,000) and works offline.

Key facts:
- Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later; Apple Silicon and Intel. Downloads are signed and notarized by Apple; disk-image size varies by release.
- macOS 26 Tahoe includes a separate recent clipboard history in Spotlight (Command+Space, then Command+4). Clipboard History also supports Sonoma and Sequoia and adds up to 10,000 searchable items, direct Shift+Command+V access, Finder file/folder references, groups, and permanent favorites.
- Captures plain text (including links and code), preserves RTF or HTML with a plain-text fallback, and stores direct PNG or TIFF clipboard images with bounded preview thumbnails. It does not perform OCR, QR recognition, or image-content search. Files and folders copied in Finder are stored by reference with previews and paste back as real Finder items.
- Instant search across text, links, and filenames; star favorites; organize clips into groups — starred and grouped clips are never auto-removed.
- Privacy: everything stays in a local SQLite file inside the app sandbox at ~/Library/Containers/app.clipboard-history/Data/Library/Application Support/Clipboard History/clipboard.sqlite. No account, no sync, no telemetry. Copies made while 1Password, Bitwarden, Dashlane, KeePassXC, Apple Passwords, Keychain Access, or LastPass is frontmost are skipped, as is content marked concealed, transient, or auto-generated on the clipboard. Ordinary unmarked secrets can still be recorded, so users can add sensitive apps to the skip list or pause recording.
- Overlay opens on the screen you're using, even over fullscreen apps. System / Light / Dark appearance. Menu-bar app with no Dock icon. Starting at login is an explicit first-run choice and can be changed in Settings; recording begins after setup is complete.
- Selecting a clip always restores it to the clipboard. Optional macOS event-posting access lets the app press Command+V automatically; without it, paste manually.
- Shortcuts: ⇧⌘V open (default, customizable) · type to search · ↑↓ navigate · ⏎ paste · ⌘1–9 paste item directly · ⌥1–9 switch tabs · ⌘D star · ⌘⌫ delete · ⌘R reveal file in Finder · ⇧⌘F Favorites tab · ⎋ close.
